subject: pathology
title: Bone tumours and metabolic bone disease

steps.tx: **Osteosarcoma** arises in adolescents at the metaphysis of the distal femur or proximal tibia, lifting periosteum into a Codman triangle with sunburst spiculation, and spreads to lungs. Biopsy precedes MAP chemotherapy with methotrexate, doxorubicin and cisplatin and limb salvage surgery, and the percentage of necrosis grades response. Secondary osteosarcoma in Paget disease of the elderly and post radiation tumours behave worse, and a painful enlarging metaphyseal mass with raised alkaline phosphatase should alarm, while MRI stages skip deposits.
steps.say: In teenagers a painful growing mass at the knee metaphysis with sunburst spiculation and a Codman triangle means osteosarcoma until proven otherwise, as the diagram shows with its lung deposits. Treatment starts with biopsy, then MAP chemotherapy and limb salvage surgery, judged by how much tumour has died. Older patients with Paget disease or prior radiation fare worse, raised alkaline phosphatase supports suspicion, and imaging stages the lungs and bone.

vis.alt: Diagram of osteosarcoma in distal femur showing Codman triangle, sunburst spiculation, and lung metastases.
vis.caption: Osteosarcoma: classic radiographic features and pulmonary metastases

steps.tx: **Ewing sarcoma** affects children at the diaphysis of femur or pelvis with onion skin periosteal layering, small round blue cells and the EWS-FLI1 translocation, and fever can mimic osteomyelitis. Multiagent chemotherapy with surgery or radiotherapy controls it, with pelvis often irradiated, and lung and marrow need staging. Chondrosarcoma in older adults at pelvis and shoulder shows rings and arcs calcification, resists chemotherapy, and needs wide resection, while dedifferentiated variants kill fast and small round blue mimics need immunophenotyping.
steps.say: A febrile child with a diaphyseal femoral mass and onion skin layering fits Ewing sarcoma, a small round blue cell tumour carrying the EWS-FLI1 fusion shown beside pelvic chondrosarcoma. Chemotherapy with surgery or radiotherapy is the backbone, and lungs and marrow must be staged. By contrast, chondrosarcoma of older adults is calcifying in rings and arcs, shrugging off chemotherapy, and demanding wide surgical clearance.

vis.alt: Side-by-side comparison of Ewing sarcoma in the femoral diaphysis with onion-skin periosteal reaction and small round blue cells versus pelvic chondrosarcoma with rings-and-arcs calcification.
vis.caption: Ewing sarcoma (onion-skin periosteum) vs chondrosarcoma (rings-and-arcs calcification).

steps.tx: Benign lesions declare themselves by age and site, led by **giant cell tumour** in the skeletally mature epiphysis as a soap bubble lytic lesion driven by RANKL and treated with denosumab and curettage. An osteochondroma points away from the joint with a cartilage cap and EXT gene background and turns malignant when the cap thickens, while enchondromas multiply in Ollier disease and pair with haemangiomas in Maffucci syndrome. Aneurysmal cysts blow out with fluid levels unlike unicameral cysts with their fallen fragment, and nonossifying fibromas sit in cortex and regress.
steps.say: An expansile epiphyseal lytic lesion in a young adult is giant cell tumour until proven otherwise, a soap bubble tumour driven by RANKL that answers to denosumab and curettage. Osteochondromas grow away from the joint under a cartilage cap that warns of change when it thickens. Remember enchondromas in Ollier and Maffucci syndromes, fluid filled aneurysmal cysts, unicameral cysts with a fallen fragment, and cortical nonossifying fibromas that quietly regress.

steps.tx: **Paget disease** remodels elderly bone into mosaic cement lines with a growing hat size, deafness, high alkaline phosphatase and a small osteosarcoma risk, treated with bisphosphonates for pain or complications. Fibrous dysplasia from GNAS mutation replaces bone with ground glass and a shepherd crook deformity, alone or in McCune-Albright syndrome with cafe au lait spots and precocity or Mazabraud syndrome with myxomas, and is observed or fixed. Osteoporosis by DEXA below minus two point five needs bisphosphonates with calcium and vitamin D, unlike osteomalacia with Looser zones and poor mineralisation.
steps.say: An elderly patient needing larger hats, losing hearing and showing very high alkaline phosphatase likely has Paget disease, where mosaic cement lines replace orderly bone and bisphosphonates ease pain. Ground glass bone with a shepherd crook deformity points to fibrous dysplasia, sometimes with cafe au lait spots and early puberty. Osteoporosis thins normally mineralised bone, while osteomalacia fails to mineralise and leaves Looser zones, so the table separates tumours from metabolic disease.
